newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada composite leading indicator - full release.
newsitem.headline: Canada composite leading indicator - full release.

text.p: The following is a full release of data from Statstics Canada.

Composite Index July 1997 The 0.8% gain in the leading index for July was little changed from the revised 0.9% advance in June, and about equal to the average monthly increases so far this year. Eight of the ten components were up, one less than in June, while one was flat. Unsmoothed, the index posted its first decrease this year, as business spending paused after breakneck gains in the first half of the year.

Employment growth in business services subsided from 0.7% to a more sustainable 0.4%. The softening of business demand was also felt in a slowdown of orders for manufactured goods and a levelling off of the shipments-to-inventories ratio. Business spending had been accelerating steadily so far this year, in line with the best gain in investment intentions since 1988.

Consumers remained reserved about spending, although the boost that employment growth has given to incomes and confidence this year provides the necessary basis for further gains. In July, housing starts snapped out of a slump that saw starts tumble 22% in the second quarter. Durable goods sales accelerated to 1%, the highest point this year.

A slowdown in the U.S. leading indicator accompanied a marked easing of growth in the second quarter. A rebound in consumer spending and a surge in employment in July are encouraging for continued growth. Available on CANSIM: matrix 191.
